title: pr-402222-dedicated-autoscaler-tokenbucket-smoothing-throughput-guarantees.json
author: Priya Raman
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets were observing short-duration request spikes that caused transient overloads and uneven serving latency. Current token-bucket-based burst controls were too aggressive/jerky when request rates oscillated; operators lacked insight into sustained throughput guarantees for a fleet during autoscale transitions. This PR introduces two complementary changes: 1) Token-bucket smoothing to make burst allowance decay and refill behavior smoother across autoscaler scale-up/scale-down windows; 2) A throughput-guarantee abstraction and reporting surface so customers can opt into per-fleet throughput commitments (tokens/sec equivalents) with observability and fallback behavior. What changed (summary): - Autoscaler core: added a smoothing layer that applies an exponential moving average to token refill rates and instantaneous consumption stats to avoid abrupt token drops on minor rate fluctuations. The smoothing window is configurable per-fleet. - Token bucket: refactored token-bucket implementation to expose refill-rate history and one-step-forecast used by the scheduler for provisional admission decisions. - Throughput guarantees: new per-fleet config fields (guaranteed_tokens_per_sec, guarantee_window_sec, guarantee_priority). When enabled, the autoscaler reserves a minimum number of tokens for the fleet during scale/transition windows. - Metrics/reporting: new metrics tokenbucket_refill_rate, tokenbucket_smoothed_rate, throughput_guarantee_active, throughput_guarantee_effective_tokens, dedicated_fleet_throughput_utilization. Added tags for fleet_id and zone. - Config CLI/API: extended dedicated API and infra-agent to accept guarantee fields; added validation to ensure guarantees don't exceed committed capacity. - Tests: unit and integration tests that simulate bursty traffic and verify smoother latency tail and guarantee enforcement. Rollout plan: feature gated behind remote flag autoscaler.tokenbucket_smoothing (default off). Throughput guarantees are opt-in per-fleet. We will enable smoothing in a canary fleet for 48h, monitor the new metrics and latency p99/p999. If stable, flip default on for all non-production fleets before enabling for production. Backward compatibility: configuration fields are additive; default behavior unchanged when flags are off. Guarantee enforcement will never allocate beyond committed capacity; when guarantees are infeasible, an operator-visible validation error is returned at config time. Migration notes: operators that opt into guarantees should run validation tooling included in this PR which simulates expected request patterns over the guarantee window. Related work: builds on previous work in PRs re: tokenbucket-smoothing and fleet-util reporting (see ENG-2902, ENG-3050). Addresses customer incident SUP-1123 where short spikes caused elevated 99th percentile latency for a critical fleet. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for smoothing and guarantee logic - [x] Integration test against autoscaler local harness - [x] Metric naming and dashboard PR (redwood/observability-pack) opened - [x] API validation and CLI docs updated Files touched (high-level): services/autoscaler/tokenbucket.go, services/autoscaler/smoothing.go, services/autoscaler/guarantee_controller.go, services/autoscaler/api/handlers.go, internal/agents/infra-agent/config.go, telemetry/metrics/registry.go, docs/dedicated/autoscaler.md, tests/autoscaler/smoothing_test.go, tests/autoscaler/guarantee_integration_test.go

release_notes: Add token-bucket smoothing for dedicated autoscaler to reduce tail latency during bursty traffic; add opt-in throughput guarantees per-fleet with validation and observability metrics.
notes_for_ops: Feature is behind feature flag autoscaler.tokenbucket_smoothing (off by default). Throughput guarantees are opt-in. Use scripts/validate-guarantee.sh before enabling on production fleets. Monitor dedicated_fleet_throughput_utilization and tokenbucket_smoothed_rate.
